notes: round 1 ran every mutant against the test file of the S03 implementation before the S03 test additions
round 2 ran the two round-1 survivors and a compiling replacement for m5, against the final test file; b2 and c6 were rerun with a fresh Zig cache because a first attempt reused a cached test binary
b2-framer-no-resync survived round 1 because the oversize record arrived in one chunk; the new test feeds it in 64-byte chunks and checks that the next record still arrives
m5-cancel-any-session did not compile (unused parameter) and was replaced by m5b, which survived until the test made another session cancel the same request id while it was in flight

c6-no-string-length still survives: the argument length check is redundant with the path, literal and item-id checks below it, and both paths report E_INVALID_ARGUMENT; it is kept because it refuses before any authorization I/O

an earlier shell version of the mutation driver reported every mutant as passing with a cached test compile because its substitutions never matched; it was replaced by mutants.py, which fails when a substitution does not match exactly once
